previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted with severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and hemobilia following obstruction of his percutaneous biliary drain. Imaging confirmed stent occlusion without pneumobilia. He underwent successful exchange of the biliary drain and stent clearance by interventional radiology, leading to improved bile flow and symptom relief. Subsequent ERCP revealed hemobilia from the right hepatic stent, prompting transfer to the ICU. Angiography identified an abnormal capsular hepatic artery supplying the bleed, which was successfully embolized. He developed transient thrombocytopenia and a low-grade fever, managed with IV antibiotics that were discontinued at discharge due to negative blood cultures. Oral vancomycin was continued for C. diff prophylaxis. His pleural effusions were deemed non-malignant. He improved clinically, with normalized liver enzymes and resolution of bleeding, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned for drain maintenance and oncology care.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old man with cholangioca s// metallic stenting. Patient
developed cholangitis and underwent placement of an int/ext biliary drain in a
jailed off segment. Patient also has perc. chole tube. Now with fevers. PTBD
drain to bag.  // PTBD check/change. Patient arriving at 9:30am to ___
for 11am procedure. Patient has been NPO.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___, Interventional Radiology Fellow and Dr.
___, attending radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
___ personally supervised the trainee during the key components of the
procedure and has reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
50 mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 32 min during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site
CONTRAST: 35 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  6.5 min, 38 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Right cholangiogram.
2. 8 mm balloon dilatation of metallic biliary stent.
3. Balloon sweeps of metallic biliary stent using ___ and 8 mm balloon.
4. Over the wire replacement of new 8 ___ destrung internal external PTBD
catheter.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The abdomen abdomen was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.

Initial scout images showed the right-sided biliary drain and percutaneous
cholecystostomy drain in appropriate, stable position.  A cholangiogram was
performed through the existing 8 ___ PTBD catheter, findings below.  The
drain was flushed and the hub of the catheter was removed.  A ___ wire was
advanced through the drain into the small bowel, and the drain was removed.  A
6 ___ sheath was advanced over the wire into the peripheral right ducts and
an antegrade sheath cholangiogram was performed, findings below.  Based on
results of this cholangiogram, decision was made to perform balloon dilatation
of the metallic biliary stent as well as balloon sweeps.

A ___ balloon was advanced over the wire into the biliary stent.  The
___ balloon was partially inflated and multiple sweeps were made through
the biliary stent.  Next, the ___ balloon was exchanged for an 8 mm
balloon.  The 8 mm balloon was advanced into the biliary stent and gentle
dilatation was performed along the length of the biliary stent.  Next, the 8
mm balloon was partially inflated and used to perform multiple sweeps through
the biliary stent.

The balloon was removed and antegrade cholangiogram through the sheath was
performed, findings below.

Based on results of these procedures and this cholangiogram, decision was made
to place a 8 ___ PTBD catheter.  The sheath was removed and a 8 ___
destrung internal external biliary drainage catheter was advanced over the
wire and positioned with side holes above and below the level of obstruction
to facilitate internal drainage.  The wire and inner stiffener were removed,
the catheter was flushed, the catheter was attached to a bag and sterile
dressings were applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications.

FINDINGS: 

1.  Initial cholangiograms demonstrated likely proximal tube occlusion, but no
intrahepatic bile duct dilatation.  The metallic biliary stent that the
catheter courses through has filling defects but maintains excellent flow of
contrast through the stent into the small bowel.
2.  Successful 8 mm balloon dilatation of the stent and balloon sweeps of the
stent with improvement, but not complete resolution of the in-stent filling
defects on post intervention cholangiogram.
3.  Successful exchange of the existing catheter with a new 8 ___ destrung
internal external biliary drainage catheter.
4.  The second metallic biliary stent and other intrahepatic bile ducts were
not seen to fill during contrast injections during this procedure. 
Significant manipulation and larger volume contrast injection of the biliary
system were avoided due to suspected biliary sepsis.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Partial patency of the existing PTBD catheter and metallic biliary stent,
with improvement of in-stent partial filling defects after balloon dilatation
and balloon sweeps.
2.  Successful exchange of existing biliary drainage catheters with new 8
___ destrung internal external biliary drainage catheter.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  If evidence of biliary obstruction persist, imaging may be
needed to determine the patency of the other biliary sent and the rest of the
biliary tree.

EXAMINATION:  MRCP

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with recurrent cholangitis; has h/o
cholangiocarcinoma, has perc chole drain as well as internal/external biliary
drain; please evaluate biliary system for any additional obstructions.  // any
intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary drainage

TECHNIQUE:  T1- and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen were
acquired in a 1.5 T magnet.
Intravenous contrast: 11 mL Gadavist.
Oral contrast:  1 cc of Gadavist mixed with 50 cc of water was administered
for oral contrast.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen from ___

FINDINGS: 

Lower Thorax: Bibasilar atelectasis with small right effusion is noted.

Liver/biliary: Left and right biliary stents are again visualized within a
internal external biliary drain and a pigtail catheter terminating in the
gallbladder.  There is again visualized mild intrahepatic biliary ductal
dilatation with foci of air within the atrophic left lobe of the liver with
multifocal stenosis.  The air within the biliary system indicates at the left
stent is patent.  Ill-defined central enhancing mass consistent with patient's
known cholangiocarcinoma is not well seen.  There are numerous foci of
arterial enhancement in the periphery of the right lobe which may be
perfusional however cholangitis is in the differential.  Mild enhancement
surrounding the dilated ducts in the left lobe also seen likely related to
cholangitis.

Pancreas: There is pancreatic ductal dilatation extending to the level of the
CBD stent which appears similar to prior examination measuring up to 5 mm.  No
focal pancreatic lesions are visualized.

Spleen: There is splenomegaly measuring up to 15.2 cm.  Trace perisplenic
fluid is noted.

Adrenal Glands: Adrenal glands are within normal limits.

Kidneys: There is a 1.7 cm simple cyst in the mid polar left kidney.  Kidneys
otherwise appear unremarkable without hydronephrosis.

Gastrointestinal Tract:  Within normal limits.

Lymph Nodes: No lymphadenopathy.

Vasculature: Within normal limits.

Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: No suspicious osseous lesions.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Mild intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation within atrophic left lobe with
multifocal areas of stenosis.  Right and left hepatic ducts stents are in
place.  Air within the left ducts indicates patency of the biliary stent. 
Mild periductal enhancement is suggestive of cholangitis.  Peripheral foci of
enhancement in the right lobe may be perfusional or related to cholangitis.
2.  Known central cholangiocarcinoma is not well visualized.
3.  Splenomegaly similar to prior.
4.  Mild pancreatic ductal dilatation to 5 mm similar to prior with pancreatic
atrophy.
